content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone will launch this autumn, reportedly named the iPhone Ultra. Here are six features worth looking forward to in this new high-end iPhone Ultra.

Design: book-style fold, titanium body, crease-free display

As Apple's first foldable product, the iPhone Ultra will feature a distinctive iPhone design.

Unlike most foldable phones, the iPhone Ultra will be wider when unfolded than when folded. It adopts a book-style folding design with an outer display that is shorter and wider in proportion, unlike any previous iPhone screen; the inner display is close in size and shape to the iPad mini.

Also differing from previous foldable phones, the iPhone Ultra's inner display is expected to feature a crease-free design—a major breakthrough for this product form.

The iPhone Ultra will borrow some design elements from the iPhone Air. It will feature a titanium frame, be extremely thin when unfolded, and when folded will resemble two iPhone Airs stacked together—but even thinner.

Display: unique size and orientation

The iPhone Ultra will come with two displays: one on the outside and another that appears only when unfolded. Rumoured sizes are as follows:

  • Outer display: 5.3 to 5.5 inches
  • Inner display: 7.6 to 7.8 inches

The outer display size is somewhat similar to the iPhone mini, but with a wider aspect ratio.

The inner display may feel very close to the iPad mini in hand.

Cameras: two rear lenses, paired with two front lenses

The iPhone Ultra will feature two rear cameras: a 48-megapixel main lens and a 48-megapixel ultra-wide lens.

This means users choosing the Ultra over the Pro models will not get a telephoto lens and its higher zoom capability.

Since the iPhone Ultra has two displays, it will also come with two front-facing cameras, one for each display.

Little is known about these cameras so far, but Apple is likely to reuse the 18-megapixel Center Stage camera introduced last year with the iPhone 17. They are expected to use a hole-punch design.

Software: iOS 27 multitasking features

iOS 27 is expected to add some iPhone Ultra-exclusive features, with details likely to be revealed only this autumn.

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, there will be two main upgrades:

  • Side-by-side multitasking apps
  • iPad-like app layouts

We can already see signs of the latter in iOS 27, with Apple adding landscape display support to several new iPhone apps.

Apple Silicon: A20 Pro chip, C2 cellular modem

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature the all-new A20 Pro chip and C2 cellular modem, both of which are also likely to appear in the iPhone 18 Pro.

The A20 Pro is reportedly a more significant upgrade than usual, adopting an all-new 2-nanometer process and using WMCM (Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module) technology to further boost efficiency.

The new chip will come with 12GB of RAM, the same as the A19 Pro. But it reportedly uses faster LPDDR5 to improve performance.

The C2 is Apple's new-generation in-house cellular modem. It is said to replace Qualcomm's 5G modem with Apple's own design, bringing several new advantages.

Touch ID

It may seem a little odd for a model named "Ultra," but Apple's foldable iPhone will not include Face ID authentication. Instead, Apple will bring back Touch ID, integrating it into the power button.

The Touch ID on the iPhone Ultra will be implemented in a way very similar to that on the iPad Air and iPad mini.

Due to the extremely thin body, Apple reportedly could not shrink the required Face ID components small enough to fit two separate modules (one for each display) into the iPhone Ultra. But future models may change that.

iPhone Ultra pricing and conclusion

Rumoured pricing for the iPhone Ultra varies widely. Most analysts expect the 256GB model to start at around US$1,999.

Whatever the final price, one thing seems certain: this will be the most expensive iPhone ever. By essentially combining a device that is both iPhone and iPad into one, Apple clearly hopes the market will accept this price.

Are you interested in buying the iPhone Ultra, or will you choose another model? Let us know in the comments.
